scenes.narration: DarkCall is a sealed-bid auction on Zcash. It proves the price without opening bids, and proves the payouts match.
Normally, auditing an auction reveals the bids, and a proven price doesn't prove the payments.
REP3 keeps bids secret-shared, coNoir proves the price jointly, and Halo2 binds every payout to it.
Now, a new auction on public testnet. Four demo bidders seal bids, each with a zero-knowledge proof and operator signatures.
Shielded deposits fund the escrow, and the operators re-check and sign the same book.
The operators compute a fresh price of thirty-five and prove it together.

scenes.band: A bidder opens its own result
scenes.narration: No operator reconstructs the bid book.
One shielded transaction pays everyone. Six Halo2 proofs bind the outputs; two-of-three FROST signs.
After confirmation, each bidder decrypts only its own receipt: a winner pays the price, a loser is refunded.
Here is a separate auction, settled on October nineteenth. Bidder one opens its receipt; bidder four, its refund.
Anyone can check its clearing price, six payouts, Zcash signatures and signed book, without a bid or viewing key.
We change the claimed price from twenty-one to twenty-two. The real verifier rejects the tampered auction proof.
Private inputs, public checks. Try DarkCall and inspect the evidence.
